sources.snippet: [Business] Item 1: Business In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, unless the context otherwise requires, references to “Realty Income,” the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us” refer to Realty Income Corporation and our subsidiaries. THE COMPANY Realty Income (NYSE: O), an S&P 500 company, is real estate partner to the world's leading companies ® . Founded in 1969, we serve our clients as a full-service real estate capital provider. As of December 31, 2025, we have a portfolio of over 15,500 properties in all 50 states of the United States ("U.S."), the United Kingdom ("U.K."), and eight other countries in Europe. We are known as “The Monthly Dividend Company ® ” and have a mission to invest in people and places to deliver dependable monthly dividends that increase over time. Since our listing on the NYSE in 1994, we have had 133 dividend increases and are a member of the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ® index for having increased our dividend for over 31 consecutive years. Our Primary Business Activities Our primary business is the acquisition, ownership, and active management of freestanding commercial properties leased under long‑term net lease agreements to a diversified base of operators, including a blend of investment grade, investment grade equivalent, and other creditworthy clients. We focus on clients with strong business models, resilient cash flow characteristics, and locations that are strategically important to their operations and aligned with our long‑term investment objectives. These activities are supported by data‑driven analytics that inform client selection, site quality, and portfolio construction. Under a net lease structure, clients are typically responsible for most or all property-level operating expenses, including real estate taxes, insurance, and maintenance, while we are entitled to receive contractually defined rental payments, many of which include embedded contractual rent escalations. The occurrence of any of the following risks could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or growth prospects or cause our actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements we have made in this report and those we may make from time to time. You should consider all of the risk factors described when evaluating our business. This “Risk Factors” section contains references to our “capital stock” and to our “stockholders.” Unless expressly stated otherwise, the references to our “capital stock” represent our common stock and any class or series of preferred stock that may be outstanding from time to time, while the references to our “stockholders” represent holders of our common stock and any class or series of preferred stock that may be outstanding from time to time. Risks Related to Our Business and Industry In order to grow, we need to continue to acquire investment properties. The acquisition of investment properties may be subject to competitive pressures. We face competition in the acquisition and operation of our properties. We expect competition from businesses, individuals, fiduciary accounts and plans, and other entities engaged in real estate investment and financing. sources.snippet: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. On November 3, 2026, the Compensation and Talent Committee (the “Committee”) of the Board of Directors of Realty Income Corporation (the “Company”) adopted the Realty Income 2026 Promote Award Plan (the “Plan”), pursuant to which certain employees of the Company and its direct or indirect subsidiaries (together, the “Company Group”), including our named executive officers, will be eligible to receive bonus awards based on the incentive allocation received by the Company Group with respect to certain investment funds, joint ventures and other investment vehicles sponsored, advised or managed by the Company Group that are designated by the Committee (each, a “Designated Fund/JV”). The purpose of the Plan is to attract, retain and incentivize certain executives and other employees of the Company Group who contribute to the investment management activities of the Company Group with respect to the Designated Funds/JVs and to promote the long-term interests of the Company and its stockholders by linking a portion of their compensation to the incentive allocation generated by the applicable Designated Fund/JV. The material terms of the Plan are described below. Eligibility and Administration. Employees of the Company Group who directly or indirectly provide services to or for the benefit of a Designated Fund/JV, as determined by the Committee, are eligible to be selected to participate in the Plan. The Plan is administered by the Committee, which may delegate its responsibilities under the Plan to one or more officers of the Company and/or one or more members of the Committee or the Board of Directors, subject to applicable laws and the limitations imposed under the Plan. The Committee has the sole discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, select participants, designate Designated Funds/JVs, determine the incentive allocation that will be the basis for each bonus pool and the amount of each bonus pool, determine each participant’s allocation of a bonus pool, set the terms of awards and make all other determinations for the administration of the Plan. Bonus Pools . In the event that a Designated Fund/JV pays an incentive allocation to the Company Group for an applicable measurement period, the Committee will establish a bonus pool, which may in no event exceed 40% of the incentive allocation for such measurement period. Multiple bonus pools may be established with respect to a Designated Fund/JV corresponding to different measurement periods or tranches of incentive allocation payments. • Percentage Allocations. The Committee will determine each participant’s percentage allocation of the applicable bonus pool, and may approve percentage allocations at, before or after the time the bonus pool is established or the incentive allocation is paid. sources.snippet: EX-99.1 2 o-991q32026.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 REALTY INCOME ANNOUNCES OPERATING RESULTS FOR THE THREE AND NINE MONTHS ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA, November 2, 2026...Realty Income Corporation (Realty Income, NYSE: O), The Monthly Dividend Company ® , today announced operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All per share amounts presented in this press release are on a diluted per common share basis unless stated otherwise. COMPANY HIGHLIGHTS : For the three months ended September 30, 2026: • Net income available to common stockholders was $403.9 million, or $0.43 per share • Adjusted Funds from Operations ("AFFO") increased 3.7% to $1.12 per share, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 • Invested $2.6 billion; our Pro-Rata Share was $2.2 billion at an Initial Weighted Average Cash Yield of 6.8% • Net Debt to Annualized Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA re was 5.4x • Achieved a Rent Recapture Rate of 103.5% on properties re-leased • Expanded our private capital platform into Europe through a strategic joint venture with KKR, supported by an initial €528.0 million investment • Issued $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of 3.750% convertible senior notes due August 2031 CEO Comments “We delivered another quarter of strong operating performance, reflecting the resilience of Realty Income’s business model, the quality of our portfolio, and the consistent execution of our team,” said Sumit Roy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Realty Income. “As a result, we are raising our 2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.45–$4.46 while reaffirming our $10.0 billion investment volume target, which is supported by a well-funded balance sheet.” “We have deliberately expanded our sources of capital and global investment capabilities, positioning us to prudently allocate capital. This quarter, we funded investments at a realized leverage-neutral spread of approximately 170 basis points and have fully prefunded our equity needs for the remainder of the year. As economic and cost of capital volatility persists, we remain focused on capital allocation while staying true to our ethos of delivering reliable, income-oriented returns for our investors.” Select Financial Results The following summarizes our select financial results (dollars in millions, except per share data): Three months ended September 30, Nine months ended September 30, 2026 2025 2026 2025 Total revenue $ 1,621.6 $ 1,470.6 $ 4,718.0 $ 4,261.4 Net income available to common stockholders (1) $ 403.9 $ 315.8 $ 1,059.7 $ 762.5 Net income per share $ 0.43 $ 0.35 $ 1.13 $ 0.84 Funds from operations available to common stockholders (FFO) (2) $ 1,041.0 $ 981.1 $ 3,031.2 $ 2,874.5 FFO per share $ 1.10 $ 1.07 $ 3.23 $ 3.18 Normalized FFO (2) $ 1,043.7 $ 994.4 $ 3,046.8 $ 2,888.4 Normalized FFO per share $ 1.10 $ 1.09 $ 3.25 $ 3.19 AFFO (2) $ 1,061.1 $ 992.0 $ 3,140.8 $ 2,889.2 AFFO per share $ 1.12 $ 1.08 $ 3.35 $ 3.19 (1) The calculati...

Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. On November 3, 2026, the Compensation and Talent Committee (the “Committee”) of the Board of Directors of Realty Income Corporation (the “Company”) adopted the Realty Income 2026 Promote Award Plan (the “Plan”), pursuant to which certain employees of the Company and its direct or indirect subsidiaries (together, the “Company Group”), including our named executive officers, will be eligible to receive bonus awards based on the incentive allocation received by the Company Group with respect to certain investment funds, joint ventures and other investment vehicles sponsored, advised or managed by the Company Group that are designated by the Committee (each, a “Designated Fund/JV”). The purpose of the Plan is to attract, retain and incentivize certain executives and other employees of the Company Group who contribute to the investment management activities of the Company Group with respect to the Designated Funds/JVs and to promote the long-term interests of the Company and its stockholders by linking a portion of their compensation to the incentive allocation generated by the applicable Designated Fund/JV. The material terms of the Plan are described below. Eligibility and Administration. Employees of the Company Group who directly or indirectly provide services to or for the benefit of a Designated Fund/JV, as determined by the Committee, are eligible to be selected to participate in the Plan. The Plan is administered by the Committee, which may delegate its responsibilities under the Plan to one or more officers of the Company and/or one or more members of the Committee or the Board of Directors, subject to applicable laws and the limitations imposed under the Plan. The Committee has the sole discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, select participants, designate Designated Funds/JVs, determine the incentive allocation that will be the basis for each bonus pool and the amount of each bonus pool, determine each participant’s allocation of a bonus pool, set the terms of awards and make all other determinations for the administration of the Plan. Bonus Pools . In the event that a Designated Fund/JV pays an incentive allocation to the Company Group for an applicable measurement period, the Committee will establish a bonus pool, which may in no event exceed 40% of the incentive allocation for such measurement period. Multiple bonus pools may be established with respect to a Designated Fund/JV corresponding to different measurement periods or tranches of incentive allocation payments. • Percentage Allocations. The Committee will determine each participant’s percentage allocation of the applicable bonus pool, and may approve percentage allocations at, before or after the time the bonus pool is established or the incentive allocation is paid.
